key_insight: YbSZ coatings create an “anomalous solid solution” that boosts zirconia’s melting point and high-temperature stability through stronger mixed bonding and more stable oxygen vacancies.
engineering_relevance: This offers a new design route for ultra-high-temperature thermal protection coatings that can survive extreme oxidation and ablation conditions beyond conventional doped oxides.
method: Compositional stabilization of ZrO2 to suppress phase instability
Mechanism linked to ionic-covalent mixed bonding and oxygen-vacancy stabilization
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a ZrO2 melting point near 2850 °C and ultimate plasma/oxyacetylene ablation resistance up to about 2780 °C and 3200 °C, respectively.
watch_item: The anomalous solid-solution strategy may be composition- and process-sensitive, so reproducibility and long-term thermal cycling stability will need validation in real service environments.
paper_title: "Anomalous Solid Solution" in Ultra-High Melting Point Oxides: A New Strategy for Developing Ultra-High Temperature Thermal Protection Coatings
